items.title: hermes-compiler npm package: publish per-platform binaries as optional packages (~40 MB unused per install)
items.body:
### Summary
The `hermes-compiler` npm package, a dependency of `react-native` (0.88.0 and current nightlies depend on `hermes-compiler@260318099.0.4`), ships `hermesc` for Windows, macOS and Linux in one package, with no `os`/`cpu` fields and no per-platform optional packages. Each install can only run one of them.

### Evidence (hermes-compiler@260318099.0.4, 49 MB unpacked)
- `hermesc/win64-bin`: ~35 MB (`icudt64.dll` 27.5 MB, `hermesc.exe` 2.6 MB, ICU and MSVC DLLs)
- `hermesc/osx-bin/hermesc`: 9.1 MB
- `hermesc/linux64-bin/hermesc`: 4.5 MB

A macOS install carries ~40 MB it cannot run, a Linux CI install ~44 MB. File listing: https://www.jsdelivr.com/package/npm/hermes-compiler?version=260318099.0.4

### Suggested fix
Publish `hermes-compiler-<os>-<cpu>` packages declared as `optionalDependencies` with `os`/`cpu` fields (the esbuild / napi-rs / swc pattern), so package managers install only the host binary. `hermes-compiler` itself would only resolve the right binary path.

### Context
Found while auditing the installed `node_modules` of the Ledger Live monorepo (https://github.com/LedgerHQ/ledger-live) to cut install size for developers and CI. Searched facebook/hermes and facebook/react-native issues for an existing report first and found none. Happy to send a PR if the approach suits you.

items.body:
### Owner

swiftlang/swift-package-manager

### Why this owner

`swift package resolve` fails in SwiftPM's dependency resolution ("exhausted attempts to resolve the dependencies graph", emitted by `Workspace` after resolution when `DependencyManifests.missingPackages` is not empty). It reproduces with the SwiftPM command-line tools of the open-source toolchains (6.4.1, the 6.4.x and main snapshots, installed with swiftly) and with SwiftPM built from `main` at 4a61be762, not only with Xcode. The manifests are valid: SE-0450 lets a package request traits on any dependency it declares, and the diagnostic is not about the manifests at all.

Read from the source (`main` at 4a61be762): `Workspace.updateEnabledTraits(for:)` (`Sources/Workspace/Workspace+Traits.swift`) records trait requests for every entry in `manifest.dependencies`, while resolution takes traits only from the edges it follows (`Manifest.dependenciesRequired(for:_:)`). An edge that no target uses therefore enables `T` for `b` in `enabledTraitsMap`, so the post-resolution check requires `c`, but resolution never expanded `b` with `T` and never fetched `c`. SwiftPM means such requests to apply: `TraitTests.traits_whenTraitUnification_whenSecondTraitNotEnabled` requests `Package10Trait2` on an edge that is guarded off and expects it enabled. So the defect is on resolution's side. Confirmed by instrumenting both sides on the original graph (below), and by a local fix in resolution. Containers report the trait requests that a manifest, at the exact version being resolved, makes on unused dependencies. The resolver applies them as traits only, never as new dependencies.

### Upstream action

New issue

### Crash signature

```text
crashed: no
requires: exhausted attempts to resolve the dependencies graph
```

### Toolchain matrix

| Toolchain | `swiftc --version` | Result |
|---|---|---|
| xcode-27.2 | Apple Swift version 6.4.2 (swiftlang-6.4.2.1.9 clang-2100.4.1.1) | reproduces |
| 6.4.1 | Apple Swift version 6.4.1 (swift-6.4.1-RELEASE) | reproduces |
| 6.4.x-snapshot-2026-10-23 | Apple Swift version 6.4.4-dev (LLVM 33d4562f9d6134f, Swift a7875ddba7eabcb) | reproduces |
| main-snapshot-2026-10-27 | Apple Swift version 6.5-dev (LLVM 7211ac1d2aee144, Swift b5fe9234c4eb9b4) | reproduces |

Local run, 2026-10-29, macOS 27.2 arm64: `issue-reduce repro.swift --require "exhausted attempts to resolve the dependencies graph" --matrix xcode-27.2,6.4.1,6.4.x-snapshot-2026-10-23,main-snapshot-2026-10-27 -- swift {}`. Also observed: SwiftPM built from `main` at 4a61be762 fails the same way.

### Regression range

Not bisected. Every toolchain tried fails; traits shipped in Swift 6.1, and the loop over `manifest.dependencies` is in all of them.

### Duplicate search

Run 2026-10-29 against swiftlang/swift-package-manager, open and closed:

```sh
gh search issues "trait unresolved" --repo swiftlang/swift-package-manager --include-prs
gh search issues "exhausted attempts traits" --repo swiftlang/swift-package-manager --include-prs
gh search issues "unused dependency traits" --repo swiftlang/swift-package-manager --include-prs
gh search issues "traits unused dependency exhausted" --repo swiftlang/swift-package-manager --include-prs
gh search issues "dependency traits not used by any target" --repo swiftlang/swift-package-manager --include-prs
gh search issues "updateEnabledTraits" --repo swiftlang/swift-package-manager --include-prs
gh search issues "trait-guarded dependency unresolved" --repo swiftlang/swift-package-manager --include-prs
gh search issues "pruneDependencies traits" --repo swiftlang/swift-package-manager --include-prs
gh search prs "traits" --repo swiftlang/swift-package-manager
gh issue list -R swiftlang/swift-package-manager --state all --search "traits in:title,body sort:updated-desc" --limit 60
gh pr list -R swiftlang/swift-package-manager --state open --limit 100   # filtered to PRs touching Workspace+Traits.swift, Workspace+Manifests.swift or PubGrubDependencyResolver.swift
```

Considered:
- swiftlang/swift-package-manager#10485 (open): "exhausted attempts" with a diamond of `path:` packages, order-dependent. A different defect: there every edge is used, and the failure is the pre-resolution pass for unversioned and branch-based packages expanding a package with the first request's traits only (recorded in `swift-issue-spm-diamond-trait-conditional-dependency`). This reproduction fails in either order and with version-based dependencies, where #10485's graph resolves.
- #10550 / #10570 (merged): carry a default-trait request into PubGrub's trait map. Present in every failing toolchain; does not touch `updateEnabledTraits`.
- #10579 (merged): repeat the workspace trait pass until no traits change. Same loop over `manifest.dependencies`; does not filter unused edges.
- #10547 / #10569 (merged): seed root manifest traits. Unrelated to edge usage.
- #8852 (merged): "Assure trait-guarded dependencies are not included in resolution; precompute enabled traits before resolution". Introduced the precomputation that this record shows disagreeing with resolution.
- #9935 (open): traits of a transitive dependency not enabled. Different symptom (too few traits, build failure), no unused edge.
- #10478 (open): hang with named and default trait requests. Different symptom.
- No open pull request touches `Workspace+Traits.swift` except release-branch merges.

Verdict: no duplicate; file a new issue.

### Minimal reproduction

```swift
#if canImport(Darwin)
import Darwin
#else
import Glibc
#endif

// root depends on b and on m. m asks for b's trait T but uses none of b's products.
// T guards b's dependency on c. Exit 1 (SwiftPM's status) when resolution fails.
let manifests = [
    "c": #"Package(name: "c", products: [.library(name: "C", targets: ["C"])], targets: [.target(name: "C")])"#,
    "b": #"Package(name: "b", products: [.library(name: "B", targets: ["B"])], traits: ["T"], dependencies: [.package(path: "../c")], targets: [.target(name: "B", dependencies: [.product(name: "C", package: "c", condition: .when(traits: ["T"]))])])"#,
    "m": #"Package(name: "m", dependencies: [.package(path: "../b", traits: ["T"])])"#,
    "root": #"Package(name: "root", dependencies: [.package(path: "../b"), .package(path: "../m")])"#,
]
var template = Array("/tmp/repro-XXXXXX".utf8CString)
let base = String(cString: mkdtemp(&template)!)
for (name, manifest) in manifests {
    mkdir("\(base)/\(name)", 0o755)
    let file = fopen("\(base)/\(name)/Package.swift", "w")!
    fputs("// swift-tools-version: 6.1\nimport PackageDescription\nlet package = \(manifest)\n", file)
    fclose(file)
}
chdir("\(base)/root")
let command: [String] = ["swift", "package", "resolve"]
execvp("swift", command.map { strdup($0) } + [nil])
```

```sh
swift repro.swift
```

### Reproduces on

main-snapshot-2026-10-27

### Reduction record

Original: swift-compositions/swift-file-system at 5a6a71b, fresh clone, with the fifteen swift-atoms packages of 2026-10-29 ("Condition each integration dependency on the traits that guard its imports") mirrored to their pre-revert commits (`swift package config set-mirror`, local clones, nothing pushed). `swift package resolve` with Xcode 27.2 fails with `* 'swift-always' from https://github.com/swift-atoms/swift-always.git`, as reported. Instrumenting SwiftPM showed `swift-serializer` required with `["Always", "Byte", "Either", "Map", "Pair", "Repetition"]` by the workspace, but expanded by resolution with `["Map", "default"]` only. The extra traits come from swift-compositions/swift-kernel, which declares swift-serializer with `traits: ["Either", "Map", "Pair", "Repetition", "Always", "Byte"]` and uses none of its products.

Reduced by hand to four packages, then mechanically: `issue-reduce repro.swift --require "exhausted attempts to resolve the dependencies graph" --jobs 4 -o reduced.swift -- xcrun swift {}`: 1232 → 1077 bytes in 2 steps, 87 runs, 2 passes, last pass kept nothing (fixed point). The two steps removed the comments and the `#else import Glibc` clause; both are kept in the record so the script also runs on Linux and says what it does.

A/B, each against the reproduction, Xcode 27.2 (observed):

| Ingredient | A (with it) | B (without it, nothing else changed) |
|---|---|---|
| `condition: .when(traits: ["T"])` on `b`'s dependency on `c` | fails | resolves |
| `traits: ["T"]` on `m`'s dependency on `b` | fails | resolves |
| `root`'s dependency on `b` | fails | resolves (`b` is then not required at all) |
| `b`'s product `B` | fails | resolves (no product, nothing to require) |
| `m` and `root` without targets or products | fails | — (already removed; with targets that do not use `B`, still fails) |
| `root` asks for `b` with `traits: ["T"]` | resolves | fails |

Not ingredients: the order of `root`'s dependencies (both orders fail), the kind of requirement (`path:`, `branch: "main"` and `from: "1.0.0"` all fail), and whether `m` uses `B` only under its own trait that is off (fails too). Swift tools version 6.1 is the first with traits.

Fix check (observed). Two earlier local attempts were dropped:
- Ignoring trait requests on unused edges in `updateEnabledTraits(for:)` broke `TraitTests.traits_whenTraitUnification_whenSecondTraitNotEnabled`.
- Seeding the workspace's trait map into the resolver and resolving again kept a dependency of a trait that 1.1 no longer enables by default: `Old` stayed checked out after an update. That is what Codex's review predicted.

The current fix is on branch [`unused-edge-traits`](https://github.com/coenttb/swift-package-manager/tree/unused-edge-traits) of the fork coenttb/swift-package-manager (ec7d54e38; first written as d619102aa on SwiftPM `main` 4a61be762). The fork also holds [`diamond-traits`](https://github.com/coenttb/swift-package-manager/tree/diamond-traits) (1adc0f29e, swiftlang/swift-package-manager#10485), [`default-request-walk`](https://github.com/coenttb/swift-package-manager/tree/default-request-walk) (063e5a9a4) and [`both-trait-fixes`](https://github.com/coenttb/swift-package-manager/tree/both-trait-fixes) (f9291ecda, the three combined for verification). No pull request is open. Containers return the trait requests that a manifest, at the exact version, revision or local state being resolved, makes on unused dependencies. PubGrub applies them as traits only. The pre-pass for branch-based and local packages uses them too. With it:
- the reproduction resolves, in its version-based, local and trait-guarded variants;
- the original swift-file-system graph resolves (97 packages pinned);
- four new `WorkspaceTests` pass, and the Workspace, PackageGraph and Trait suites run with no failures.

Three of the new tests fail on `main`. The fourth, an update after a trait stops being a default, passes on `main` and fails on the dropped seeding attempt.

Independent review (a fresh agent given only the upstream draft, 2026-10-29): it reproduced the failure on main-snapshot-2026-10-27 and Xcode 27.2. It tried removing c's product and target, b's products, targets, target dependency and trait condition, m's traits, and root's dependency on b or on m, and it tried root requesting T. Every removal resolves except c's contents. Two things it raised, and what was decided:
- `c` reduced to `Package(name: "c")` still fails. This is not adopted. Once fixed, that graph would fail later with "product 'C' not found", so the reproduction would no longer show the expected result. c's product and target are kept so that a fixed SwiftPM resolves it cleanly.
- When m has a target that uses `B`, it still fails. That is expected here: with `path:` dependencies, that graph hits the separate diamond defect (`swift-issue-spm-diamond-trait-conditional-dependency`, swiftlang/swift-package-manager#10485). The version-based variant of it resolves, and the version-based unused-edge variant fails. So "unused" is the ingredient of this defect, and the draft's framing stands.

Independent review: reproduced on main-snapshot-2026-10-27; tried every package, field, dependency and trait removal; nothing left to remove (c's contents only, rejected above).

### Upstream draft

**Title:** Traits requested on a dependency that no target uses leave the dependency they guard unresolved

### Description

A package declares a dependency with a trait but uses none of its products. SwiftPM still turns the trait on, so a dependency that the trait guards is required, but resolution never follows the unused edge and never fetches it. Resolution fails with "exhausted attempts".

`Workspace.updateEnabledTraits(for:)` records trait requests for every entry in `manifest.dependencies`, as `TraitTests.traits_whenTraitUnification_whenSecondTraitNotEnabled` expects. Resolution, however, takes traits only from the edges it follows (`manifest.dependenciesRequired(for:_:)`), so it never expands `b` with `T`. The same happens when the dependency is used only by targets guarded by traits that are off. It does not depend on order, and it happens with version-based, branch-based and `path:` dependencies.

### Expected behavior

`swift package resolve` succeeds: `T` is enabled on `b`, as SwiftPM computes it, and `c` is resolved.

### Actual behavior

```
error: exhausted attempts to resolve the dependencies graph, with the following dependencies unresolved:
* 'c' at /tmp/repro-XXXXXX/c
```

### Steps to reproduce

The script writes four packages: `c`; `b`, whose trait `T` guards its dependency on `c`; `m`, which depends on `b` with `traits: ["T"]` and has no targets; and `root`, which depends on `b` and `m`. It then runs `swift package resolve` in `root`.

```swift
#if canImport(Darwin)
import Darwin
#else
import Glibc
#endif

// root depends on b and on m. m asks for b's trait T but uses none of b's products.
// T guards b's dependency on c. Exit 1 (SwiftPM's status) when resolution fails.
let manifests = [
    "c": #"Package(name: "c", products: [.library(name: "C", targets: ["C"])], targets: [.target(name: "C")])"#,
    "b": #"Package(name: "b", products: [.library(name: "B", targets: ["B"])], traits: ["T"], dependencies: [.package(path: "../c")], targets: [.target(name: "B", dependencies: [.product(name: "C", package: "c", condition: .when(traits: ["T"]))])])"#,
    "m": #"Package(name: "m", dependencies: [.package(path: "../b", traits: ["T"])])"#,
    "root": #"Package(name: "root", dependencies: [.package(path: "../b"), .package(path: "../m")])"#,
]
var template = Array("/tmp/repro-XXXXXX".utf8CString)
let base = String(cString: mkdtemp(&template)!)
for (name, manifest) in manifests {
    mkdir("\(base)/\(name)", 0o755)
    let file = fopen("\(base)/\(name)/Package.swift", "w")!
    fputs("// swift-tools-version: 6.1\nimport PackageDescription\nlet package = \(manifest)\n", file)
    fclose(file)
}
chdir("\(base)/root")
let command: [String] = ["swift", "package", "resolve"]
execvp("swift", command.map { strdup($0) } + [nil])
```

```sh
swift repro.swift
```

It resolves if `b` drops the trait condition, if `m` drops `traits: ["T"]`, or if `root` asks for `T` itself.

### Swift Package Manager version/commit hash

`main` at 4a61be762, and the toolchains below. The code is the same on `release/6.4.2` and `release/6.4.x`.

### Swift & OS version

macOS 27.2, arm64:

| Toolchain | `swift --version` | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Xcode 27.2 | Apple Swift version 6.4.2 (swiftlang-6.4.2.1.9 clang-2100.4.1.1) | fails |
| 6.4.1 | Apple Swift version 6.4.1 (swift-6.4.1-RELEASE) | fails |
| 6.4.x snapshot 2026-10-23 | Apple Swift version 6.4.4-dev (LLVM 33d4562f9d6134f, Swift a7875ddba7eabcb) | fails |
| main snapshot 2026-10-27 | Apple Swift version 6.5-dev (LLVM 7211ac1d2aee144, Swift b5fe9234c4eb9b4) | fails |

### Readiness

- [x] The reproduction is one file and one command, and uses no Institute code or third-party package.
- [x] The matrix was run with the minimal reproduction, on toolchains installed from swift.org or the stated Xcode.
- [x] The duplicate search covered open and closed issues and pull requests in the owner's repository.
- [x] An independent reviewer reproduced it from the draft alone and found nothing left to remove.

### Filing record

Approved by Coen: 2026-10-29. His words: "File 1 and 2" (1 is this issue, 2 is the #10485 comment).

Filed: https://github.com/swiftlang/swift-package-manager/issues/10749
Related comment on the diamond defect: https://github.com/swiftlang/swift-package-manager/issues/10485#issuecomment-6507892031

items.title: [Proposal]: MySQL Package & Extension Manager

labels.name: Extensibility/Ecosystem
labels.description: Extensions, integrations, plugins, and ecosystem opportunities.

items.body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched existing GitHub issues and did not find a duplicate proposal.
- [x] I have removed or redacted sensitive information.

### Primary Contact Name

Alex Gaetano Padula

### Primary Contact Email

agpadula@tidesdb.com

### Company / Organization

TidesDB Corp.

### Role

Founder, CEO & Chief Architect

### Additional Authors / Contributors

_No response_

### Component

Server

### Target Release (Optional)

MySQL 26.7.0 and later

### Roadmap Section

Extensibility/Ecosystem

### Related Issues / Pull Requests / References (Optional)

_No response_

### Executive Summary

MySQL has one of the broadest extension surfaces of any relational database with eleven and growing implemented
plugin interfaces, pluggable storage engines with real alternatives, loadable functions, and a
component service registry in which one component may re-implement another's service. It has no
distribution mechanism for any of it.

Installing an out-of-tree extension today requires the operator to obtain the MySQL source tree at
the exact version they are running, place the extension inside it, configure and build the whole
server, and copy the resulting shared object into `plugin_dir` by hand. This is not a gap in
tooling; it follows from three properties of the server:

1. *Storage engine plugins are bound to one exact server version.*
   `MYSQL_HANDLERTON_INTERFACE_VERSION` is defined as `(MYSQL_VERSION_ID << 8)`, and
   `sql_plugin.cc` sets both the lower and upper bound of its check from it, so the comparison
   collapses to equality. A plugin built against 26.7.0 is refused by 26.7.1 with *"API version for
   STORAGE ENGINE plugin is too different"*. Patch releases count.
2. *No development headers ship with the server.* An installed 26.7.0 prefix contains only client
   headers (`mysql_com.h`, `errmsg.h`, `field_types.h`, `mysql/`). There is no `handler.h` and no
   `mysql/plugin.h`, so no extension of any kind can be compiled against an installed server.
3. *Plugins can only be loaded from one directory, by bare filename.*
   `INSTALL PLUGIN ... SONAME` passes the library name through `check_valid_path()`, which rejects
   any string containing a directory separator.

This proposal adds the missing layer, a package format, a compatibility key that makes artifact
reuse safe, a resolver that prefers verified pre-built binaries and falls back to building from
source, and a SQL surface for installing, updating and removing packages. It also proposes the two
small server changes without which none of it is possible - shipping the plugin SDK headers, and
publishing the build identity an artifact must match.

Two findings shape this proposals design:

- *Only three of the eleven plugin interfaces are version-locked* (storage engine, daemon,
  information schema). The other eight carry their own interface-version constants that change only
  when that interface changes. A package of a portable kind can be published once and serve many
  server releases, so the expensive per-release build matrix applies to a minority of packages.
- *MySQL's component loader is already scheme-dispatched and the scheme handler is itself a
  replaceable service.* `file://` is implemented, `builtin://` is reserved with no implementation,
  and the loader resolves a scheme by acquiring the service named `dynamic_loader_scheme_<scheme>`.
  A `pkg://` scheme therefore requires no change to the server at all. This has been prototyped and
  works.

### User / Developer Stories

- *As a DBA deploying an alternative storage engine*, I want to install it with one statement
against the server I already run, rather than reproducing the vendor's build environment.

- *As a DBA planning a minor upgrade*, I want to know *before* I upgrade which of my installed
extensions have no artifact for the new server version, because today a 26.7.0 >> 26.7.1 upgrade
silently invalidates every version-locked plugin and the server starts with tables it cannot open.

- *As an extension author*, I want to build against an installed server the way a PostgreSQL
extension author builds against `pg_config`/PGXS, instead of distributing instructions that begin
"clone the MySQL source".

- *As a security-conscious operator*, I want extension installation to be an audited, separately
privileged action against an allow-listed registry with signature verification, rather than "copy
this `.so` into `plugin_dir` as root".

- *As a platform integrator*, I want a declared dependency graph, because real engines are not
self-contained - TideSQL links `libtidesdb` and pins it by major version, and a manager that ignores
native dependencies has solved the easy half of the problem.

- *As a MySQL maintainer*, I want the extension ecosystem to grow without the server taking on
responsibility for third-party code, so the trust boundary and the privilege model must be explicit.

### Proposed Scope

- A package manifest format (_TOML_) describing a package's identity, kind, server compatibility,
  native dependencies, prebuilt artifacts and source build recipe.
- A *compatibility key* - server version, platform, toolchain ABI, build type - that determines
  whether a given artifact may be loaded into a given server.
- A resolver that selects a version satisfying both the request and the server, prefers a verified
  pre-built artifact, and falls back to building from a tagged source checkout.
- Installation support for the extension kinds MySQL already has registries for:
  plugins (`mysql.plugin`), loadable functions (`mysql.func`) and components (`mysql.component`).
- A SQL surface with `INSTALL PACKAGE`, `UPDATE PACKAGE`, `REMOVE PACKAGE`, `SHOW PACKAGES`,
  `SHOW PACKAGE STATUS`.
- A `mysql.package` system table recording, per installed package, the resolved version, the full
  key it was installed for, the constraint originally requested, and the artifact digest.
- A `pkg://` dynamic loader scheme service for components.
- Pre-upgrade compatibility reporting driven by `mysql.package`.
- Two server-side prerequisites - ship the plugin SDK headers and a CMake package; publish the build
  identity (including the numeric version id and the ABI-affecting flag set).

### Out of Scope / Future Work

- *Operating a public registry (maybe on https://planet.mysql.com/)?.* This specifies the client/server mechanism and the manifest format, not who hosts an index or funds a build farm.
- *Packages that carry SQL objects.* PostgreSQL extensions install SQL objects with versioned
  upgrade scripts. That would make loadable-function and information-schema packages considerably
  more useful and is a natural second phase, but it reopens the upgrade-script design question and
  is deliberately excluded here.
- *Sandboxing the build helper beyond process isolation.* A first version runs builds
  out-of-process and unprivileged; container or seccomp confinement is future work.
- *Cross-version artifact compatibility.* Nothing here attempts to create a stable
  storage-engine ABI. The proposal works within the exact-version rule rather than changing it.
- *Automatic rebuild on server upgrade.* The proposal reports and stages; it does not silently
  rebuild extensions during an upgrade.
- *Windows and macOS packaging specifics.* The design is platform-neutral and the key has a
  platform field, but only Linux x86-64 has been exercised in prototypes.

### References

| Source | What it establishes |
|---|---|
| `include/mysql/plugin.h:665` | `MYSQL_HANDLERTON_INTERFACE_VERSION (MYSQL_VERSION_ID << 8)` |
| `include/mysql/plugin.h:115-127` | The twelve plugin type slots; slot 0 (UDF) unimplemented |
| `sql/sql_plugin.cc:404-425,1063` | Per-type version bounds; the "API version … too different" check |
| `sql/sql_plugin.cc:569,664` | `check_valid_path()` rejecting directory separators |
| `components/libminchassis/dynamic_loader.cc:160-205` | URN `scheme://path`; `file://` and reserved `builtin://` |
| `components/libminchassis/dynamic_loader.cc` (`get_scheme_service_from_urn`) | Scheme resolved as `dynamic_loader_scheme_<scheme>` |
| `components/libminchassis/dynamic_loader_scheme_file.cc:160-168` | The duplicate-library guard a scheme must implement |
| `components/libminchassis/registry.cc:256` | `set_default()` a component may re-implement another's service |
| `include/mysql/components/services/dynamic_loader.h:282-303` | The `dynamic_loader_scheme` service definition |
| `scripts/mysql_system_tables.sql:195,203,361` | `mysql.func`, `mysql.plugin`, `mysql.component` |
| `sql/sys_vars.cc:5147-5155` | `version_compile_machine`, `version_compile_os` |

### Functional Requirements

| # | Requirement |
|---|---|
| F1 | A package manifest shall declare name, version, kind, license, server compatibility, native dependencies, zero or more prebuilt artifacts keyed by compatibility key, and an optional source build recipe. |
| F2 | The resolver shall compute the running server's compatibility key from the server itself, not from configuration. |
| F3 | The resolver shall select the highest package version satisfying both the operator's constraint and the server's key; `latest` shall mean *latest compatible*, not latest published. |
| F4 | For a version-locked kind the compatibility specification shall be an exact server version; for a portable kind it shall be a range. |
| F5 | Where a prebuilt artifact matches the key, its digest shall be verified before use, and its manifest signature shall be verified against configured trust roots. |
| F6 | Where no prebuilt artifact matches and source fallback is permitted, the resolver shall obtain the declared source at the declared tag and run the manifest's named build recipe. |
| F7 | Installation shall dispatch by kind `INSTALL PLUGIN` for plugins and storage engines, `CREATE FUNCTION … SONAME` for loadable functions, `INSTALL COMPONENT` for components. |
| F8 | `mysql.package` shall record resolved version, full key, requested constraint, and artifact digest for every installed package. |
| F9 | `UPDATE PACKAGE` shall re-resolve under the *recorded* constraint unless the operator supplies a new one, so an update cannot cross a major boundary implicitly. |
| F10 | The prior artifact shall be retained across an update so a failed load can be rolled back to a known-good file. |
| F11 | Removing a storage engine package shall be refused while tables in that engine exist. |
| F12 | A pre-upgrade check shall resolve every row of `mysql.package` against a nominated target server version and report packages with no matching artifact. |
| F13 | A failed resolution shall report the compatibility key that was sought and the keys that exist, not merely "not found". |
| F14 | Native dependencies declared in `[requires]` shall be resolved, and a missing or incompatible dependency shall fail the install before anything is staged. |


### Non-functional Requirements

| # | Requirement |
|---|---|
| N1 | *No implicit network access.* The registry allow-list shall be empty by default; a server never configured for packages shall not reach the network. |
| N2 | *No unsigned code.* An unsigned package or an unknown signer shall be refused, with no override option. |
| N3 | *Separate privilege.* Package installation shall require its own dynamic privilege, not `SUPER` and not `INSTALL PLUGIN`, default-granted to nobody. |
| N4 | *No compilation inside `mysqld`.* Source builds shall run in a separate unprivileged process with no database access. |
| N5 | *Auditability.* Every install, update and removal shall emit an audit event carrying the resolved key and artifact digest. |
| N6 | *Failure containment.* A failed build or a failed load shall leave the server running and the previous state intact. |
| N7 | *No new steady-state cost.* Resolution runs only on explicit operator action; there shall be no background polling or periodic registry contact. |
| N8 | *Determinism.* Given the same manifest, key and digest, installation shall be reproducible. |


### Impact Areas

- [x] SQL syntax or statements
- [x] Configuration options or system variables
- [x] Command-line options or utilities
- [x] User-visible behavior
- [x] Observability
- [x] Security or privilege model
- [ ] Protocol or replication behavior
- [x] Upgrade / downgrade compatibility
- [ ] Performance or resource usage
- [x] Files, persistence, or metadata formats
- [x] APIs or internal interfaces
- [x] Testing or QA coverage needs

### Summary of the Approach


An extension artifact is addressed by a *compatibility key* with four fields:

```
tidesdb/2.0.0 @ mysql-26.7.0 / linux-x86_64 / gcc13-cxx11abi / release
               └─ server ─┘   └─ platform ─┘   └─ toolchain ─┘  └ build ┘
```

Each field corresponds to a demonstrated failure mode rather than defensive over-specification:

| Field | Why it is in the key |
|---|---|
| `server` | Exact `MYSQL_VERSION_ID` for version-locked kinds; a declared range for portable kinds. |
| `platform` | OS and architecture. |
| `toolchain` | C++ ABI generation and symbol floor. A plugin built on a current Ubuntu requires `GLIBC_2.34` and will not load on RHEL 8 however correct its server version. |
| `build` | Release vs debug. `NDEBUG` changes server struct layouts the extension compiles against. |

Resolution prefers a verified prebuilt artifact and falls back to a source build. The server drives
the operation through SQL; the work of fetching, verifying and building is delegated to a separate
process. Installed state lives in `mysql.package`, which is what makes updates and pre-upgrade
checks possible.

### User Interface

```sql
-- install
INSTALL PACKAGE 'tidesdb';                      -- latest compatible with this server
INSTALL PACKAGE 'tidesdb' VERSION '2.0.0';      -- exact
INSTALL PACKAGE 'tidesdb' VERSION '^2.0';       -- range
INSTALL PACKAGE 'tidesdb' FROM 'vendor-registry';

-- update, re-resolving under the recorded constraint
UPDATE PACKAGE 'tidesdb';
UPDATE PACKAGE 'tidesdb' VERSION '2.1.0';       -- move the constraint deliberately

-- remove
REMOVE PACKAGE 'tidesdb';

-- inspect
SHOW PACKAGES;
SHOW PACKAGE STATUS 'tidesdb';
SELECT * FROM mysql.package;
```

Components additionally become installable through the existing loader with no new syntax, by
registering a scheme service:

```sql
INSTALL COMPONENT 'pkg://some_component@1.2';
```

### Configuration / Knobs


| Variable | Scope | Default | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| `package_registry_allowlist` | Global, dynamic | *empty* | Registries the server may contact. Empty means packages are disabled. |
| `package_trust_roots` | Global, startup | *empty* | Public keys that may sign manifests and artifacts. Never read from a registry. |
| `package_store_dir` | Global, startup | `<basedir>/pkg` | Where verified component artifacts are staged. |
| `package_allow_source_build` | Global, dynamic | `OFF` | Whether the source fallback may run on this host. |
| `package_build_timeout` | Global, dynamic | 600 s | Upper bound on a source build. |

New read-only variables publishing the build identity (prerequisite, see §5):

| Variable | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `version_id` | The numeric `MYSQL_VERSION_ID` the plugin loader actually compares. *Not currently exposed* - only `@@version` as a string, which may carry a suffix. |
| `build_toolchain` | Compiler and C++ ABI tag the server was built with. |
| `build_type` | `release` / `debug`. |
| `sdk_cxxflags`, `sdk_ldflags` | The ABI-affecting flag set an extension must be built with. |

### Observability

- *`mysql.package`* - one row per installed package >> name, resolved version, kind, compatibility
  key, requested constraint, artifact digest, install timestamp, source (`binary` or `source`).
- *`SHOW PACKAGE STATUS <name>`* - resolved version against available versions, whether an update
  is available under the recorded constraint, and whether a staged-but-pending artifact exists.
- *Audit events* - one per install, update and removal, carrying resolved key and digest, so
  extension installation is reviewable after the fact.
- *Error log* - resolution failures name the key sought and the keys available; build failures
  include the helper's captured output, truncated.
- *Performance Schema (optional)* - stages for `resolve`, `fetch`, `verify`, `build`, `stage`,
  `load`, so a slow install is attributable.


### User Procedure


Installing an engine on a server that has a matching prebuilt artifact:

```sql
mysql> SET GLOBAL package_registry_allowlist = 'https://pkg.example';
mysql> GRANT INSTALL_PACKAGE ON *.* TO 'dba'@'localhost';
mysql> INSTALL PACKAGE 'tidesdb';
mysql> SELECT * FROM mysql.package;
mysql> CREATE TABLE t (id INT PRIMARY KEY) ENGINE=TidesDB;
```

Preparing for a server upgrade:

```sql
mysql> SHOW PACKAGE STATUS FOR SERVER '26.7.1';
+---------+---------+------------------+--------------------------------+
| package | version | target_available | note                           |
+---------+---------+------------------+--------------------------------+
| tidesdb | 2.0.0   | NO               | no artifact for mysql-26.7.1   |
| connlog | 1.0.0   | YES              | portable kind, range satisfied |
+---------+---------+------------------+--------------------------------+
```

The operator stages the new-key artifacts before upgrading, so the upgraded server finds its
extensions already present rather than starting with unloadable plugins.

### Security Considerations


Server-driven installation is the most useful shape and the most dangerous. It gives `mysqld`
outbound network access and, on the source path, a compiler. Four containments, all mandatory:

1. *Trust.* Manifests and artifacts are signed; the server verifies against trust roots configured
   at startup, never material supplied by the registry. An unsigned or unknown-signer package is
   refused with *no override flag* - an override becomes the documented workaround.
2. *Privilege.* `INSTALL_PACKAGE` is its own dynamic privilege, default-granted to nobody, and is
   not implied by `SUPER` or `INSTALL PLUGIN`. Installing a package is strictly more dangerous than
   loading a file an administrator already placed on the host.
3. *Network.* `package_registry_allowlist` is empty by default. There is no implicit default
   registry, so a server that is never configured for packages cannot be induced to fetch anything.
4. *Build isolation.* The source path never compiles inside `mysqld`. `mysql_package_build` runs
   as a separate unprivileged process with no database connection, a scratch directory, and the
   named recipe from the manifest. On hosts with no toolchain the helper is absent and the source
   path reports that plainly.

Residual risks that should be stated rather than designed away, a signed package is still arbitrary
code in the server's address space; the registry operator is a trusted party; and the build helper
executes a recipe from a manifest, which is why `package_allow_source_build` defaults off and why a
binary-only first version is a reasonable scope reduction.

### Compatibility and Behavior Changes

- *No change to existing extension loading.* `INSTALL PLUGIN`, `CREATE FUNCTION … SONAME` and
  `INSTALL COMPONENT 'file://…'` behave exactly as before.
- *New system table.* `mysql.package` requires a dictionary upgrade step. A downgrade leaves the
  table present and unused.
- *The plugin SDK becomes a published interface.* This is the significant new commitment, once
  headers ship, their contents become something third parties build against. The SDK should
  therefore carry its own version and an explicit stability statement - in particular that it offers
  *no* cross-version guarantee for the version-locked kinds, matching the loader's existing rule.
- *Replication.* Unaffected; package state is local to a server.
- *Upgrade hazard addressed, not introduced.* A server version change already invalidates every
  version-locked extension. This proposal makes that visible and recoverable instead of leaving it
  to be discovered at startup.


### Block Diagram

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["INSTALL PACKAGE 'tidesdb'"] --> B["Privilege check: INSTALL_PACKAGE"]
    B --> C["Read compatibility key from this server"]
    C --> D["Resolve version: constraint AND server compat"]
    D --> E["Verify manifest signature against trust roots"]
    E --> F["Resolve native dependencies from [requires]"]
    F --> G{"Prebuilt artifact<br/>for this key?"}
    G -- yes --> H["Verify sha256"]
    G -- no --> I{"package_allow_source_build?"}
    I -- no --> J["Fail: report key sought + keys available"]
    I -- yes --> K["mysql_package_build:<br/>unprivileged, no DB access"]
    K --> L["Run named recipe against SDK"]
    L --> H
    H --> M["Stage into plugin_dir or package_store_dir"]
    M --> N{"kind"}
    N -- "plugin / storage_engine" --> O["INSTALL PLUGIN"]
    N -- loadable_function --> P["CREATE FUNCTION ... SONAME"]
    N -- component --> Q["INSTALL COMPONENT 'pkg://name'"]
    O --> R["Record in mysql.package + audit event"]
    P --> R
    Q --> R
```

### Interface Specification

*Manifest format.* TOML, one file per package version.

```toml
[package]
name        = "tidesdb"
version     = "2.0.0"
kind        = "storage_engine"      # selects the version-locking rule
plugin_name = "TidesDB"          # what INSTALL PLUGIN registers
soname      = "ha_tidesdb.so"
license     = "GPL-2.0"
maturity    = "beta"

[compat]
server = "=26.7.0"               # exact storage engines are version-locked
                                            # an audit plugin would write server = ">=8.0.0"

[requires]
libtidesdb = "^10.1.1"           # native dependency, major pinned

[[binary]]
key    = "mysql-26.7.0/linux-x86_64/gcc13-cxx11abi/release"
url    = "https://pkg.example/tidesdb/2.0.0/…"
sha256 = "…"

# for multiplatform / architecture 
[[binary]]
key    = "mysql-26.7.0/linux-aarch64/gcc13-cxx11abi/release"
url    = "https://pkg.example/tidesdb/2.0.0/linux-aarch64.so"
sha256 = "…"

[[binary]]
key    = "mysql-26.7.0/macos-arm64/clang17-libc++/release"
url    = "…"
key    = "mysql-26.7.0/macos-arm64/clang17-libc++/release"
url    = "…"
sha256 = "…"

[[binary]]
key    = "mysql-26.7.0/windows-x64/msvc193/release"
url    = "…"
sha256 = "…"

[source]
git      = "https://github.com/tidesdb/tidesql-mysql"
tag      = "v2.0.0"
build    = "./install.sh --rebuild-plugin --mysql-src ${MYSQL_SDK_SRC}"
produces = "ha_tidesdb.so"
```

`kind` is what lets the resolver apply the right version rule without the manifest restating it.
`[source]` is a *named recipe*, not an arbitrary shell string, so the build helper has something it
can constrain.

*`mysql.package` system table.*

| Column | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | `varchar(64)` PK | Package name |
| `version` | `varchar(32)` | Resolved version |
| `kind` | `varchar(32)` | `storage_engine`, `plugin`, `loadable_function`, `component` |
| `compat_key` | `varchar(255)` | Full key the artifact was installed for |
| `constraint_spec` | `varchar(64)` | Constraint originally requested |
| `artifact_sha256` | `char(64)` | Digest of the staged artifact |
| `origin` | `enum('binary','source')` | How it was acquired |
| `installed_at` | `timestamp` | Install time |
| `pending_version` | `varchar(32)` NULL | Staged update awaiting restart |

*The `pkg://` scheme service.* No core change is required. The loader resolves a scheme by name:

```c
/* components/libminchassis/dynamic_loader.cc, get_scheme_service_from_urn */
size_t scheme_end = urn.find("://");
my_string scheme(urn.begin(), urn.begin() + scheme_end);
my_service<SERVICE_TYPE(dynamic_loader_scheme)> service(
    (my_string("dynamic_loader_scheme_") + scheme).c_str(),
    &imp_mysql_minimal_chassis_registry);
```

A component providing `dynamic_loader_scheme_pkg` therefore extends a *running* server. The service
name is declared as an alias of the service type, exactly as the built-in file scheme does:

```c
typedef SERVICE_TYPE_NO_CONST(dynamic_loader_scheme)
    SERVICE_TYPE_NO_CONST(dynamic_loader_scheme_pkg);

BEGIN_SERVICE_IMPLEMENTATION(pkg_scheme, dynamic_loader_scheme_pkg)
pkg_load, pkg_unload END_SERVICE_IMPLEMENTATION();
```

> The scheme contract carries an invariant the service definition does not express. The
> definition is only `load` and `unload`, but a scheme implementation *must* refuse to load the
> same library twice. The built-in file scheme guards on the address of the library's
> `list_components` entry point (`dynamic_loader_scheme_file.cc:160-168`); without that guard the
> same component is registered twice and the second unload frees state the first still references.
> A first prototype that omitted it crashed the server with SIGSEGV. If the scheme mechanism is to
> be opened to third parties, this contract must be specified, or a helper supplied that enforces
> it.

*The plugin SDK.* Measured from the compiler's own dependency output, not estimated:

```
storage engine header closure          366 headers,  5.1 MB
  include/ 188   sql/ 97   libs/ 69   sql-common/ 4   extra/ 4   vector-common/ 1
  generated 3 - my_config.h, mysql_version.h, mysqld_error.h   (configuration-specific)

+ component service headers           +161 headers
union across extension kinds              527 headers
```

Three properties of the SDK follow:

1. `libmysqlservices.a` already ships. It supplies `mysql_malloc_service` and
   `plugin_registry_service`, and is already installed into the prefix. Only the headers are
   missing, which makes this ask smaller than it appears.
2. The flag set is part of the ABI. A complete engine compiled and linked cleanly but would not
   load until built with the server's own `-ftls-model=initial-exec`, `-D_FILE_OFFSET_BITS=64` and
   `-Wl,-Bsymbolic-functions`. Publishing a toolchain *tag* is insufficient; the flags themselves
   must be published.
3. The SDK must be a union, not a sample. The storage-engine closure appeared to be a superset -
   it already contained `plugin_audit.h`, `udf_registration_types.h` and
   `component_implementation.h` - yet a component failed to compile, because a storage engine never
   includes any `components/services/*.h`.


### Proposed Implementation Plan


The ordering is chosen so that each phase is independently useful and the riskiest work comes last.

| Phase | Work item | Server change | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Ship the plugin SDK, 527 headers, the generated configuration headers, and a CMake package for out-of-tree builds. Publish the SDK's own version and stability statement. | Install rules + packaging | Prerequisite; validated by building a complete storage engine, an audit plugin, a loadable function and a component against a staged SDK with no source tree |
| 2 | Publish the build identity with numeric `version_id`, toolchain tag, build type, and the ABI-affecting compile/link flag set as read-only variables. | New read-only sysvars | Gap confirmed - no numeric version id is currently exposed |
| 3 | `pkg://` dynamic loader scheme service, shipped as a component, plus a written scheme contract or an enforcement helper. | None | **Prototyped and working**; a component installed through `pkg://` appears in `mysql.component` |
| 4 | `mysql.package` system table, the `INSTALL_PACKAGE` dynamic privilege, audit events, and the configuration variables. | Dictionary + privilege + sysvars | Designed |
| 5 | Parser and runtime for `INSTALL/UPDATE/REMOVE PACKAGE` and `SHOW PACKAGE[S]`, binary path only (verified prebuilt artifacts). | Parser + runtime | Resolution logic prototyped client-side |
| 6 | `mysql_package_build` helper and the source fallback, behind `package_allow_source_build=OFF`. | New helper binary | Prototyped client-side - git clone at tag >> build against SDK >> stage >> install |
| 7 | Pre-upgrade compatibility reporting (`SHOW PACKAGE STATUS FOR SERVER`). | Runtime | Designed |


### QA Notes


### Correctness and refusal paths

| Scenario | Expected |
|---|---|
| Install a version-locked package whose artifact key names a different server patch release | Refused before staging, naming the key sought and the keys available |
| Artifact digest does not match the manifest | Refused; nothing staged |
| Manifest unsigned, or signed by a key not in `package_trust_roots` | Refused; no override path exists |
| Registry not in `package_registry_allowlist` | Refused without network contact |
| `package_allow_source_build=OFF` and no binary matches | Refused with a clear reason, not a silent build |
| Source build exits non-zero, times out, or produces no artifact | Statement fails; server unaffected; previous state intact |
| `REMOVE PACKAGE` for a storage engine with live tables | Refused - requires asking the engine, not the file system |
| `UPDATE PACKAGE` where the newest version violates the recorded constraint | No update performed; reported as already current |
| Update whose new artifact fails to load | Rolls back to the retained previous artifact |
| Install a package already installed | Idempotent or clearly refused; never double-registered |

### Scheme-specific

| Scenario | Expected |
|---|---|
| Same library loaded via `file://` and `pkg://` | Second load refused by the duplicate-library guard |
| `pkg://` URN naming an absent artifact | Clean failure, no crash |
| `UNINSTALL COMPONENT` then reinstall through the same URN | Succeeds; no stale registration |
| Scheme component unloaded while a `pkg://` component is loaded | Defined behaviour required; currently undefined |

### Cross-version and upgrade

| Scenario | Expected |
|---|---|
| Start a server one patch release newer with version-locked packages installed | Pre-upgrade check lists them; post-upgrade repair path reports them rather than failing silently |
| Staged `pending_version` applied at restart | New artifact loads; `mysql.package` updated |
| Downgrade below the version that created `mysql.package` | Table unused; no errors |

### Automation opportunities

- The refusal matrix above is mostly table-driven and suits `mysql-test-run` with a fixture registry
  served from the test's own directory, no network needed.
- Cross-version refusal can be tested without a second server build by publishing a manifest whose
  artifact key names a fabricated version; the loader's check is what is under test.
- The duplicate-library guard deserves a dedicated crash-regression test, since it is an invariant
  a third-party scheme must honour and a prototype has already violated it.
- Digest and signature failures should be tested with deliberately corrupted artifacts rather than
  mocks, since the whole value of the key is that it is checked against reality.

### Known gaps in current validation

- Only Linux x86-64 has been exercised. The platform and toolchain fields of the key are designed but
  untested on macOS and Windows.
- Signature verification is specified but not implemented in the prototype; only digests are checked.
- The server-driven surface (`INSTALL PACKAGE`) is designed and not implemented; the prototype drives
  installation from a client, which is the same resolution logic in a different process.
- `libtidesdb`-style native dependency resolution is declared in the manifest format and checked for
  presence only; version-range satisfaction across a dependency graph is not implemented.

items.title: Add the OS, the distribution and the package managers to the system prompt
items.body:
## The problem

The system prompt tells the model very little about your machine. This is the full text that it sends today:

```
The shell is $shell on $platform
```

The value of `$platform` comes from `platform.system()`. On all Linux machines that value is the word `Linux`.

The word `Linux` is not sufficient. Many commands are different on different Linux distributions. The most frequent example is the installation of a package:

- On Ubuntu the command is `sudo apt install foo`.
- On Fedora the command is `sudo dnf install foo`.
- On Arch Linux the command is `sudo pacman -S foo`.
- On Alpine the command is `sudo apk add foo`.

The model must guess. Frequently it guesses `apt`, because `apt` is the most common in its training data. The guess is wrong for approximately one half of the users.

There is a second problem. The model does not know about WSL (Windows Subsystem for Linux). In WSL, some commands behave in a different way. As an example, a command for the systemd service manager can fail.

## Where this idea comes from

The fork `c0ffee0wl/llm-cmd-comp` has this feature. These are the related commits:

- `08b2acf` — Added OS environment detection
- `2c79c19` — Tweaked OS environment detection
- `2fe0626` — refactor(system): extract detection logic to new module

The fork adds a new file, `llm_cmd_comp/system_info.py`, with 154 lines. The file has four detection functions.

**Important: do not copy the file without a change.** Read the sections below. There are three changes to make.

## The plan

Add a new module `llm_cmd_comp/system_info.py`. Use the module in the system prompt.

### Step 1: Write the detection module

Write these four functions:

| Function | Result | Method |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `detect_shell()` | A tuple: the name and the version | The `SHELL` and `PSModulePath` environment variables |
| `detect_os()` | A text, as an example `Linux (Ubuntu)` | `platform.system()`, then the `NAME=` line of `/etc/os-release` |
| `detect_environment()` | `native`, `wsl`, `gitbash` or `cygwin` | The `WSL_DISTRO_NAME` and `MSYSTEM` variables, and `/proc/version` |
| `detect_package_managers()` | A list of names | `shutil.which()` for each name in a list |

You can use the code of the fork as your start. Get it from this address:

<https://raw.githubusercontent.com/c0ffee0wl/llm-cmd-comp/main/llm_cmd_comp/system_info.py>

### Step 2: Make three changes to the code of the fork

**Change 1 — Make the list of package managers shorter.**

The fork looks for 22 package managers. The list contains the language package managers `pip`, `pipx`, `uv`, `npm`, `cargo` and `gem`. Almost all developer machines have some of these. Therefore they give almost no information to the model. But they make the prompt longer, and you pay for each token.

Keep the system package managers only:

```python
PACKAGE_MANAGERS = [
    "apt", "dnf", "yum", "pacman", "zypper", "apk",   # Linux
    "snap", "flatpak",                                 # Universal Linux
    "brew", "port",                                    # macOS
    "choco", "scoop", "winget",                        # Windows
    "nix", "guix",                                     # Alternative
]
```

These are the names that solve the problem in the first section.

**Change 2 — Do not use a bare `except`.**

The code of the fork has two bare `except:` statements. A bare `except` catches all exceptions. This includes `KeyboardInterrupt`. Then the user cannot stop the program with Ctrl-C.

Write the specific exception:

```python
try:
    with open("/etc/os-release") as f:
        ...
except OSError:
    pass
```

**Change 3 — Do not keep the unused function.**

The fork has a function `get_system_context()`. It puts all results in a dictionary. Nothing calls this function. Do not add it. You can add it later, if some code needs it.

### Step 3: Change the system prompt

Change `SYSTEM_PROMPT` in `llm_cmd_comp/__init__.py`. Add the new information. Also add three sentences from the fork. They make the answer of the model better:

```
Return only the command to be executed as a raw string, no string delimiters
wrapping it, no yapping, no markdown, no fenced code blocks, what you return
will be passed to the shell directly.

Environment: $shell_display on $os_display$env_suffix$pkg_suffix

If there is a lack of details, provide the most logical solution.
Ensure the output is a valid shell command for the environment.
If multiple steps are required, try to combine them using '&&'.

For example, if the user asks: undo last git commit
You return only: git reset --soft HEAD~1
```

The fork adds this text to the sentence about `&&`: `(For PowerShell, use ';' instead)`. Do not add that text. This repository has no PowerShell integration file. The text is not necessary, and it makes the prompt longer.

Then replace the function `render_default_prompt()`. The new function puts the values in the template:

```python
def render_default_prompt():
    shell_name, shell_version = detect_shell()
    environment = detect_environment()
    package_managers = detect_package_managers()
    return SYSTEM_PROMPT.substitute(
        shell_display=f"{shell_name} {shell_version}".strip(),
        os_display=detect_os(),
        env_suffix=(
            f" [running in {environment.upper()}]" if environment != "native" else ""
        ),
        pkg_suffix=(
            f"\nPackage managers: {', '.join(package_managers)}"
            if package_managers
            else ""
        ),
    )
```

The fork uses `safe_substitute()`. Use `substitute()`. `substitute()` raises an error if a value is absent. This shows you a bug immediately. `safe_substitute()` hides the bug, and the model receives the text `$env_suffix`.

### An example of the result

On an Ubuntu machine in WSL the prompt contains this line:

```
Environment: bash on Linux (Ubuntu) [running in WSL]
Package managers: apt, snap
```

## About the speed

`detect_package_managers()` calls `shutil.which()` 15 times. Each call looks in all directories of your `PATH`. This is fast. It is some milliseconds in total. The request to the model takes some seconds. Therefore the user does not see the difference.

Do not add a cache for this. It is not necessary, and a cache can become old.

## How to test the change

There is no unit test framework in this repository at this time. Do a manual test.

1. Add a temporary `print()` of the result of `render_default_prompt()`. Run `llm cmdcomp "test"`. Look at the text. Remove the `print()` after the test.
2. Run the same test in WSL, if you have WSL. The text `[running in WSL]` must be visible.
3. Type `install ripgrep` and press Alt-Backslash. On Fedora the result must use `dnf`. On Ubuntu the result must use `apt`.
4. On a machine with no `/etc/os-release` file, the function must return `Linux` and must not fail.
5. Run `./test_integration.sh`. It must pass. This test builds the wheel. It shows that the new file is in the package.

## Notes for the person who does the work

- Use these commit messages: `feat: detect the OS, the distribution and the package managers` and `feat: improve the system prompt`. Two commits are better than one. They are two different subjects.
- The change is approximately 100 new lines and 20 changed lines.
- Do not copy `CLAUDE.md` from the fork. Do not copy the `.gitignore` file of the fork. They are for that fork only.

items.title: Proposal: support bun install for faster, smaller installs (no runtime change)
items.body:
A lot of the work on Kong Royale now runs through coding agents, which clone and install the repo many times, often several checkouts side by side on one machine. I measured whether Bun's package manager helps with that, and whether Bun as a runtime is worth it. In short, the package manager helps, mostly with disk space, and needs nothing from you. The runtime doesn't, because it changes the simulation's results.

**Measurements.** All on one machine: Linux x86_64, 4 vCPU, Node 22.23.4, npm 10.9.9, Bun 1.4.4. Runs were interleaved, and each tool had its own empty cache for the cold runs.

| | `npm ci` | `bun install --frozen-lockfile` |
|---|---|---|
| Install, cold cache (5 runs, median) | 1.94 s | 0.26 s |
| Install, warm cache (5 runs, median) | 1.61 s | 0.05 s |
| `node_modules` | 140 MB | 130 MB |
| Disk for one checkout, cache included | 180 MB | 130 MB |
| 8 checkouts installed in parallel: wall time | 6.0 s | 0.12 s |
| 8 checkouts installed in parallel: extra disk | 1.21 GB | 7.5 MB |
| `npm run build` / `npm test` | pass / 11 of 11 | pass / 11 of 11 |
| `dist/` | | byte-identical to the npm install |

Bun reads `package-lock.json` directly and installs the same versions. The one exception is sharp's unused WebAssembly fallback, which it skips. It writes no `bun.lock`, and it refuses to run if `package.json` and the lockfile disagree.

The disk saving comes from hardlinking out of Bun's global cache (on macOS, `clonefile`). That only helps checkouts on the same disk, not separate machines. The time saved is under 2 s per install, so disk is the real gain.

**Runtime: not proposed.** Under Bun, most things work and are faster: server boot, `ws`, `netlab --check`, the build, and 11 of 11 tests. But the simulation produces a different match. `sim-smoke trios 42` gives state hash `d802631a` under Bun, against `c8f3110c` under Node. The cause is that JavaScriptCore's `Math.sin`, `cos`, `atan2`, `exp`, `pow` and others return different last bits from V8's, and `shared/sim` uses them. Each runtime is deterministic on its own, but a Bun server would not reproduce Node's matches. So the runtime stays Node.

**Proposal**
1. **Docs only (the PR linked below).** Document `bun install --frozen-lockfile` as an optional alternative to `npm ci`. npm stays the source of truth for dependencies, and everything runs on Node. Nothing changes in `package.json`, the lockfile or CI.
2. **Optional follow-up, if you want it guarded.** A small CI job that runs `bun install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts` (with `oven-sh/setup-bun` pinned to a commit), then the existing build and test on Node. It would catch a lockfile that Bun can't read. Happy to send it if you'd like.

**Not proposed:** replacing `package-lock.json` with `bun.lock`. That would make Bun required for everyone.

**Risks**
- Bun only runs install scripts for trusted packages. esbuild and sharp work as they are, and build and test pass.
- On Linux and Windows, hand-editing a file in `node_modules` also edits the cached copy shared with other checkouts.
- So far I've verified this on Linux only.

If you'd rather keep the project npm-only, that's fine too. Contributors can still use Bun locally without any change on your side.

items.title: Pin all dependencies and audit the toolchain for speed
items.body:
## What

Two passes over every dependency, the toolchain and the CI actions:

1. **Pin everything** so builds are reproducible and a bad upstream release can't land without a PR.
2. **Audit every package for speed**: pick the fastest tool that fits Pheeme's goals of quick CI, a fast dev loop and a small, fast app, and drop anything unused.

## Part 1: pinning

Current state: both lockfiles are committed (`package-lock.json`, `src-tauri/Cargo.lock`) and `rust-toolchain.toml` exists, but:

- `package.json` uses ranges everywhere (`^2`, `^18`, `^0.577.0`, ...).
- `Cargo.toml` uses semver ranges, and CI doesn't pass `--locked`, so `cargo` can quietly update the lock.
- GitHub Actions are pinned to moving major tags (`actions/checkout@v7`, `tauri-apps/tauri-action@v1`, `mitchellh/vouch/...@v1`, ...).
- Nothing keeps pins current (no Renovate or Dependabot).

Tasks:
- [ ] npm: exact versions in `package.json` and `save-exact=true` in `.npmrc`, so new installs stay exact.
- [ ] Rust: `--locked` on every `cargo` call in CI and release. (`Cargo.toml` ranges can stay because `Cargo.lock` is the pin for an app, but CI must refuse to change it.)
- [ ] Toolchain: `rust-toolchain.toml` set to an exact version (not `stable`), plus a Node version in `.nvmrc` / `engines` that CI reads.
- [ ] Actions: pin every third-party action to a full commit SHA with a `# vX.Y.Z` comment.
- [ ] Add Renovate with grouped weekly PRs, a **minimum release age** (e.g. 3 days) as a supply-chain guard, and automerge for patch updates of dev tools once CI is green.
- [ ] Optional: `cargo-deny` (advisories, licenses, duplicate crates) and `npm audit signatures` in CI.

## Part 2: speed audit

For each item: keep it or swap it, and note why in the PR.

### Package manager
- [ ] **npm → pnpm or bun.** Faster `install`/`ci`, a strict `node_modules`, and pnpm has `minimumReleaseAge` built in. (On this devbox, pnpm already goes through the `heavy` job-slot shim.)

### Lint / format / typecheck
- [ ] **ESLint → oxlint.** It's 50–100× faster and has native `react-hooks` and `typescript` rules. Keep ESLint only for a rule oxlint lacks, if any, using `eslint-plugin-oxlint` to turn off the rules both cover. Keep `scripts/check-tokens.mjs`.
- [ ] Formatter: there is none today. Add **oxfmt** or **Biome** (both fast) instead of Prettier.
- [ ] Typecheck: try **`tsgo`** (TypeScript native preview) in CI alongside `tsc`, and switch once it's stable for our code.

### Build / test
- [ ] **Vite 6 → latest**, and evaluate **rolldown-vite** (Rust bundler) for build time.
- [ ] `@vitejs/plugin-react` → **`@vitejs/plugin-react-swc`** (or the oxc variant) for faster transforms.
- [ ] **Vitest 2 → latest** (also fixes the exact `@vitest/coverage-v8@2.1.9` mismatch risk).
- [ ] **jsdom → happy-dom** for faster tests, if our tests pass on it.
- [ ] `cross-env`: only sets one env var for `tauri`. Check whether it can go.

### Runtime deps (bundle size / startup)
- [ ] **`date-fns` appears unused in `src/`.** Remove it, or use `Intl.DateTimeFormat` / `Intl.RelativeTimeFormat`.
- [ ] `@types/dompurify`: DOMPurify 3 ships its own types, so remove it.
- [ ] React 18 → 19 (+ React Compiler) and Zustand 4 → 5: worth it for render performance?
- [ ] `lucide-react`: confirm per-icon imports so it tree-shakes; check bundle size with `vite-bundle-visualizer`.

### Rust
- [ ] `tokio` `features = ["full"]` → only the features we use (faster compiles, smaller binary).
- [ ] Unused crates: run `cargo-shear` / `cargo-machete`.
- [ ] Bumps: `thiserror` 1 → 2, `rand` 0.8 → 0.9, and duplicate crates in the tree (`cargo tree -d`).
- [ ] Release profile: `lto = "thin"`, `codegen-units = 1`, `strip = true`, `opt-level` review. Measure binary size and startup before and after.
- [ ] CI: **cargo-nextest** for tests, the **mold** (Linux) / **lld** linker, and check `Swatinem/rust-cache` hit rates.

## How to decide

Measure before and after each swap: CI wall time per job, `npm ci` / install time, lint time, test time, `vite build` time, bundle size, release binary size. Put the numbers in each PR. Swap only when it's clearly faster and nothing breaks. Feeds into #47 (perf CI), which can track the same numbers.

## Done when
- Every dependency, toolchain and action is pinned, and Renovate keeps the pins current.
- Each item above is checked off as swapped, kept (with reason) or removed.

items.title: chore: add Lua linting and focus AGENTS.md on intent
items.body:
## Summary

Add a lightweight Lua lint step and revise `AGENTS.md` so that machine-checkable rules are enforced by lint or tests, while the guide focuses on design intent and practical contributor instructions.

## Linter proposal

Evaluate Selene as the first CI lint candidate. It is written in Rust, but contributors do not need Rust installed if they use a prebuilt executable from a pinned GitHub Release; the current release publishes Linux, macOS, and Windows archives. Cargo is the upstream documented installation path and does require Rust, so contributor docs should point to a release archive or a supported package manager rather than requiring Cargo. The release archive should be unpacked to obtain the CLI.

- [Selene installation docs](https://kampfkarren.github.io/selene/cli/installation.html)
- [Selene releases](https://github.com/Kampfkarren/selene/releases)

Compare this with Luacheck before deciding: Luacheck explicitly supports LuaJIT 2.x, but its installation path may involve LuaRocks and its dependencies. Confirm Selene's standard-library/configuration fit for this Neovim project and pin the chosen linter version in CI. Keep the local workflow simple and document the install command.

## Move guarantees to executable checks

Use tests for semantic or runtime properties that a linter cannot establish, including:

- compile does not mutate input and repeated compilation is deterministic;
- spec surface, accepted shapes, and explicit rejection behavior;
- dependency, condition, priority, and ref/range semantics;
- startup versus post-startup activation and exactly-once sourcing;
- trigger cleanup/replay, module preload behavior, and `VeryLazy` timing.

Use lint for static issues it can reliably detect, such as syntax errors, undefined globals, and unused locals. Configure Neovim/test globals deliberately instead of suppressing broad warning classes.

## `AGENTS.md` revision

Shorten the guide by keeping the project purpose, scope boundaries, core design principles, key workflow hazards, and commands contributors need. Replace detailed behavioral inventories with links to the authoritative design docs and named tests. Keep concise reminders for invariants whose breakage is especially costly, but make the test the source of truth for the exact behavior.

## Acceptance criteria

- A pinned linter runs locally and in CI on the relevant production and test Lua files.
- The lint command and installation instructions are documented; no Rust toolchain is required if Selene is selected.
- Existing lint findings are resolved or narrowly documented with rationale.
- Each machine-checkable `AGENTS.md` rule maps to a test or lint check; uncovered important invariants receive tests.
- `AGENTS.md` is shorter and links to the docs/tests that own the detailed behavior.
